title: Subnetting a block
summary: Split a network into N equal subnets, or size a subnet for N hosts.

steps.title: Borrowing bits
body: To split a block into **N** equal subnets, **borrow** host bits for the network: `b` bits give `2^b` subnets, so `b = ceil(log2 N)` and the new prefix is `prefix + b`.
`10.0.0.0/24` into 4 subnets: borrow 2 bits, so /26, each 64 addresses:
> **Practise:** the **Subnetting trainer** in the app generates endless random drills like these.

steps.prompt: This counts the bits to borrow from a /24 for N subnets. What does it print?
steps.explain: You can only split in powers of two. 3 subnets costs as much as 4.

steps.prompt: Arrange the four /26 subnets of `192.168.1.0/24` in address order.
steps.explain: Each starts 64 after the previous one.

steps.title: Sizing by hosts
body: Going the other way, you need **h** hosts: find the smallest host-bit count `n` with `2^n - 2 >= h`. The prefix is `32 - n`.
| Hosts needed | Host bits | Prefix | Usable |
Watch the edges: 30 hosts fit a /27 exactly, 31 do not.

steps.prompt: What is the smallest subnet for each host count?
You must carve `192.168.1.0/24` into 6 department subnets of up to 25 hosts each. Which prefix?
steps.explain: 6 subnets need 3 borrowed bits (/27), which leaves 5 host bits = 30 hosts. Both constraints fit.

steps.title: Split a block
prompt: Write `List<string> Split(string cidr, int n)` returning all `2^b` subnets (where `2^b` is the smallest power of two >= n) in address order.
Throw `ArgumentException` if the new prefix would exceed /32. Helpers are given.
starter: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
solution: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
if (np > 32) throw new ArgumentException("block too small");
for (long i = 0; i < (1L << bits); i++) result.Add($"{FromUInt((uint)(net + i * size))}/{np}");
hints: Count bits with `while ((1 << bits) < n) bits++`.
Subnet i starts at `network + i * 2^(32 - newPrefix)`.

steps.title: Size for hosts
prompt: Write `int PrefixForHosts(int hosts)`: the longest prefix (smallest subnet, up to /30) whose usable host count is at least `hosts`.
Throw `ArgumentException` if even a /1 can't hold them.
